record.paper_title: Research Problems on Relations Between Nijenhuis Geometry and Integrable Systems
record.original_question: For a candidate integrable PDE system, is the system bi-Hamiltonian, and if it is, what is its second Poisson structure? In particular, does it fit the BKM pattern where the compatible Poisson structures are third order?

evidence.quote: TQ1 Is the system bi-Hamiltonian? What is the second Poisson structure? (In the BKM systems, compatible Poisson structures are of third order).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. A Nijenhuis operator on a smooth manifold $M^n$ is a (1,1)-tensor field $L$ whose Nijenhuis torsion $N_L(X,Y) := L^2[X,Y] - L[LX,Y] - L[X,LY] + [LX,LY]$ vanishes identically. A Nijenhuis operator $L$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$ is called differentially nondegenerate if the differentials of the coefficients of its characteristic polynomial are linearly independent on an open dense set. Given such an operator, one can associate a family of evolutionary PDE systems on the loop space of $\mathbb{R}^n$, called Bogoyavlensky–Kupershmidt–Manakov (BKM) systems; these include, for $n=1$, the KdV, Harry Dym, Camassa–Holm and Dullin–Gottwald–Holm equations, and, for $n\ge 2$, Kaup–Boussinesq, coupled KdV, coupled Harry Dym and multi-component Camassa–Holm equations. Each BKM system is known to admit a Hamiltonian formulation with a Poisson operator of third order in $\partial_x$.

A Hamiltonian PDE system $u_t = P_1\,\delta H_1/\delta u = P_2\,\delta H_2/\delta u$ is called bi-Hamiltonian if $P_1$ and $P_2$ are two compatible Poisson operators (i.e.\ every linear combination $\lambda P_1 + \mu P_2$ is again Poisson).

Problem. Let $\mathcal S$ denote a candidate integrable evolutionary PDE system constructed from a differentially nondegenerate Nijenhuis operator on $\mathbb{R}^n$ via the BKM procedure. 
(a) Determine whether $\mathcal S$ is bi-Hamiltonian.
(b) If so, find an explicit second Poisson operator $P_2$ compatible with the canonical (third-order in $\partial_x$) Poisson operator $P_1$ of $\mathcal S$.
(c) Establish whether $\mathcal S$ fits the BKM pattern in which both compatible Poisson operators $P_1, P_2$ are differential operators of third order.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open research problem (a "test question") in the program connecting Nijenhuis geometry to integrable systems. Existing literature discusses bi-Hamiltonian structures for individual BKM-type equations (KdV, Camassa–Holm, Kaup–Boussinesq, etc.) but a general answer establishing bi-Hamiltonianity and an explicit second third-order Poisson operator for all BKM systems associated with arbitrary differentially nondegenerate Nijenhuis operators does not appear to be available. Status appears open.

status_evidence.title: On the bi-Hamiltonian structure of Bogoyavlensky system
status_evidence.snippet: Bi-Hamiltonian structure of specific Bogoyavlensky systems studied.
status_evidence.claim: Bi-Hamiltonian structures for particular subclasses are known, but a uniform answer for general BKM systems is not provided.
